_why: Invariant 3 of CLAUDE.md says a number on this site is a claim with an owner, and until
2026-08-04 it carried `(not enforced)` beside it. On that day two numbers on the trailryx
page were found stale by a week (1,031 tests where the repository ran 1,064), and one on the
tokenfuse page was stale by 196 (513 where the workspace runs 709). Neither was wrong when
written. That is the whole problem: a figure on a marketing page has no owner and no clock.
This file gives every one of them both. `scripts/service-numbers.sh` refuses a push whose
pages disagree with what is written here, and reports loudly on entries nobody has ever
reproduced or has not reproduced recently.
It CANNOT check that a recorded value is still true: this repository has no access to the
other repositories' test suites. What it makes impossible is the silent case, a number
changed on a page with nothing recording where it came from. `status` says which of those
two situations each entry is in, and lying in it is the only way to defeat this.

entries.command: cargo test --workspace, summed; and ./scripts/readme-numbers.sh, which gates the same figure inside that repository
entries.note: The strongest entry here: the repository refuses its own push when this number drifts, so the site only has to keep up with a figure that is already true.

entries.command: cargo test --all, summed over every `test result` line
entries.note: Found stale by this file's own first run: the page said 513 and `cargo test --all` sums to 709. The gap, not the number, is why this file exists, so it is recorded here rather than only in git history. Unlike trailryx, this repository has no gate on its own README figure, so nothing but this entry will notice the next drift.

The repository's own README says 22 in two places and its VALIDATION reports three of twenty-two firing under load, so the site and the source agree. No command reproduces the figure: the detectors are not enumerable by a grep that would still be right next month. Recorded as agreement rather than as measurement, because those are different things and only one of them survives a refactor.

pytest is not installed on the machine this was written on, so the number has never been reproduced here. Counting `def test_` gives about 457, which is indicative and not authoritative: parametrised tests multiply and some files are not collected. Not written into the page on the strength of a grep.
Same as engram. A grep counts about 276, which is far enough from 217 to be worth a real run rather than a correction made from a guess.

entries.command: xcodebuild test, count from the result bundle
entries.note: The repository is not checked out on this machine, so nothing here has ever seen this figure.
Entries of what, and counted by whom, is not recorded anywhere this file can reach. The first job of a gate is to make that visible rather than to guess.
